title: Eureka Stockade
summary: On 3 December 1854 a government force attacked a stockade built by a few hundred diggers at Ballarat, Victoria, after months of unrest on the goldfields over the licence tax, official corruption and a police and soldier licence hunt on 30 November. Many lives were lost and the government was condemned; the event is remembered as shaping Australian democracy.

uncertainty.note: Single-day battle. The unrest ran from months earlier; the licence hunt that sharpened it was on 30 November 1854 (Ballarat Reform League).

as_recorded.value: battle on 3rd December (months of unrest culminated on Thursday 30th November 1854)

where.modern_name: Eureka Stockade site, Eureka Street, Ballarat East, Victoria, Australia

importance.justification: A goldfields uprising credited with a major influence on Australia's development as a democracy.

reviewer_note: Death toll is not stated on either opened page and is left out; other sources give differing totals. "A few hundred" defenders is the Reform League wording only. Coordinates are Wikidata's point for the stockade, which the City of Ballarat page places at the Eureka Stockade site; accuracy of the exact stockade line is not asserted.
